 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Camouflage, flashy kicks and a mustache that deserves its own starting lineup.
 The San Antonio Spurs brought plenty of personality to the Frost Bank Center on Wednesday night, Nov. 4, ahead of their showdown with the Dallas Mavericks.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement From designer sneakers to statement graphic tees, the Silver and Black made sure their pregame fashion was anything but ordinary.
 Here's a closer look at what five Spurs players wore before tipoff.
 Forget wearing flashy clothes, Keldon Johnson's mustache might have been the biggest fashion statement of the night.
 The reigning Sixth Man of the Year arrived sporting a playful mustache that looked straight out of a 1970s detective show, giving his pregame appearance a little extra character.
 Johnson wore a white VALE FOREVER "Air Donald" graphic tee featuring Ronald McDonald soaring toward a basketball hoop, layered beneath a light-gray zip-up hoodie. He paired the outfit with blue jeans, Bottega Veneta Orbit low-top sneakers, and his signature "KJ" chain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Now, Stephon Castle kicked things off in a Boredom Kills Trust camouflage long-sleeve sweatshirt featuring a large graphic across the chest.
 The Spurs guard paired the sweatshirt with light-wash blue jeans and a cross necklace, keeping his look casual while letting the camouflage do the talking.
 It looks like Castle's "Area 51" teammate, Victor Wembanyama, also got the camouflage memo.
 At 7-foot-4, blending into a crowd isn't exactly Wembanyama's specialty, but the Spurs superstar gave it a shot Wednesday night, wearing a black zip-up hoodie layered beneath a Nike Tech Dri-FIT Woven Camo Windrunner Oversized Jacket in Neutral Olive and Black.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He completed the look with gray Nike joggers and olive-green Nike sneakers, keeping things comfortable with an outdoors-inspired ensemble.
 With his hood up and hands tucked into his pockets, Wembanyama looked ready for a covert mission rather than an NBA matchup.
 Spurs guard Dylan Harper kept things coordinated in a forest-green Nike hoodie and matching sweatpants layered over a black T-shirt.
 He completed the outfit with black Nike sneakers and his signature diamond-encrusted No. 2 chain, adding some sparkle to his otherwise understated look.
 Between laid-back camouflage fits and colorful sweats, Johnson personality stands out the most as the Spurs get ready to face their in-state rival, the Dallas Mavericks.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Tipoff is scheduled for 8:30 p.m.
